segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Iran talks, Nvidia's CEO, a new chief of staff
bullets: Trump: Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress; Rubio: no breakthrough
Nvidia's board investigates its own CEO
Stephen Miller's first day as chief of staff; Hegseth impeachment vote looms
Kraków gunman dies in hospital

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Monday, November ninth. The president says new strikes on Iran are highly unlikely, if talks progress. His secretary of state says the talks are nowhere near a breakthrough.
The board of Nvidia has opened an investigation into its own chief executive. Houthi missiles put glass on a sidewalk in Riyadh. And one drone switched off most of the electricity in Iraqi Kurdistan.
Stephen Miller starts today as White House chief of staff, the House may vote this week on impeaching the defense secretary, and the Kraków gunman has died. A lot today. Let's go.

segments.strap: TRUMP: IRAN STRIKES 'UNLIKELY'; RUBIO: NO BREAKTHROUGH
segments.headline: Two messages from one government, and Tehran's answer

graphic.title: Strikes, talks and the strait

stats.label: Targets named by Trump incl. bridges

bullets: Trump: new strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress
Rubio: Iran's demands 'outrageous and ridiculous'
Task Force Iron Gate 'in full force'
IRGC claim: strait navigation aids destroyed (unconfirmed)

sources.name: Gulf News (Iron Gate, Xi and Putin)

lines.text: Here is the U.S. side, in the president's own words. Trump said a renewed attack on Iran is highly unlikely if the talks progress and Iran signs, quote, a very strong agreement. He also said he would authorize strikes if needed, and that the U.S. has identified targets, including thirty-eight bridges.

Now the same government, a few hours later. Secretary of State Rubio said Iran's demands are, quote, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic, and that the sides are not on the verge of a breakthrough. He called the war not necessarily popular, but necessary to stop a nuclear threat. Those are his claims.

Trump also posted that Task Force Iron Gate is, quote, in full force and effect. Central Command says its job is to block weapons, dual-use technology and sanctioned goods across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Tehran calls it wordplay, and another failed attempt to force a collapse.

On the water, here is Iran's account. An unnamed Guard official told state media that navigation aids in the southern strait were destroyed, and that no unauthorized ship passed overnight. Reuters carried it. There is no U.S. or shipping-industry confirmation. Iran also says tankers hit mines. Its counts run from two to four.

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said mediator travel paused after the U.S. midterms. Qatar's prime minister is due at the White House today at noon Eastern. One report says Qatar floated inspections in exchange for ending the blockade. There is no sign either side agreed.

Two more claims. An Iranian official said a U.S. attack on Qeshm Island on Sunday night did no major damage. There was no U.S. statement. And Trump says he expects to discuss Iran with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at next week's summit.

Markets heard the word unlikely. Brent slipped to about ninety-seven dollars in Monday trading in Asia, after falling sixteen percent last week. The betting market on a final U.S.-Iran nuclear deal by year's end still sits at nine and a half percent.

segments.strap: HOUTHI MISSILES HIT ARAMCO TOWER; DRONE CUTS KURDISTAN POWER
segments.headline: Riyadh's glass, Kurdistan's lights, and Erbil's flood

graphic.title: Saudi Arabia and Iraq
bullets: Aramco office tower in Riyadh damaged by debris; no casualties
Khor Mor gas field drone hit; no claim of responsibility
Erbil flood: three dead, 300+ rescued (governor)
Iraq says U.S. understanding on an oil shipping lane (claim)

lines.text: Saudi Arabia says its air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles and two cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh and the south. Falling debris damaged an Aramco administrative building in the financial district. The Energy Ministry calls the damage minimal and reports no casualties.

A Reuters witness and verified video show blown-out windows across several floors. The Houthi spokesman claims six operations, naming Aramco sites and Riyadh airport. Those are his claims. The reports reviewed show interceptions and the building damage, not an impact at the airport.
In Yemen, Houthi-run health authorities say the death toll from Saturday's strikes near Sanaa has risen to forty-four. That figure comes from the Houthi Health Ministry, as AP attributes it.

Next door in Iraq, one drone hit a gas storage tank at the Khor Mor field and started a fire. Production stopped. The Kurdistan electricity ministry says about twenty-eight hundred megawatts went offline. That is roughly two-thirds of the region's power, from one outlet.

Hospitals and water stations stayed up on hydropower and backup units. No casualties were reported in the preliminary count. Nobody has claimed it. Iraq's prime minister ordered a joint investigation with the Kurdistan government.

The same region had a second problem. In Erbil, the governor says flooding killed three people and more than three hundred were rescued. The city's water treatment plants were stopped because the river was too muddy to treat. That is the flood, not the drone.

And a claim to watch. Iraq's foreign minister told Al Jazeera that Iraq reached an understanding with the United States to move oil through Hormuz by a lane near Oman. He put the war's losses at sixty billion dollars. There is no U.S. confirmation.

segments.strap: NVIDIA BOARD INVESTIGATES CEO JENSEN HUANG OVER TIES TO SUSPECTED SPY
segments.headline: The chipmaker that is the A.I. trade investigates its own founder

graphic.title: A board inquiry, not a finding
bullets: Huang told staff he had an affair with a Megaspeed executive
NYT: U.S. intelligence says China's M.S.S. recruited her
Board: 'no reason to believe' secrets were compromised
No government confirmation of the intelligence claim

lines.text: On Sunday, Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into its chief executive, Jensen Huang. A committee of independent directors, with outside counsel, will run it. The board statement announces an investigation. It does not announce a finding.

Here is what is on the record. Huang told employees in an email that he had an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore company. The New York Times reports that U.S. intelligence assessed that China's Ministry of State Security recruited her to gather information on him. The U.S. government has not confirmed that.

The board says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. China calls the reports baseless and purely slanderous smears. The chairs of three House committees cite significant national security concerns and want to question him.

Markets shrugged, for now. Asian chip stocks bounced on Monday and Nvidia shares rebounded, per investing reports. But every futures write-up named the probe as the overhang. A bad week for a company holding up an entire stock market.

segments.strap: MILLER'S FIRST DAY AS CHIEF OF STAFF; TRUMP: DEPORTATIONS 'TOO TOUGH'
segments.headline: A new chief of staff, and a president second-guessing his signature policy

graphic.title: The Miller White House
bullets: 60 Minutes: deportation policy 'might be too tough'
Rep. Stutzman (R-Ind.): fire people, including Miller
Dana White meets Trump today 'on other matters'
Senators McCormick, Johnson seek delay of GOP leadership vote

lines.text: Stephen Miller takes over as White House chief of staff today. Reporting calls the promotion a sign of a more combative approach after the election losses.

And here is the timing. In an interview recorded Friday and aired Sunday on 60 Minutes, Trump said his deportation policy, quote, was too tough. He said it might be too tough, and that it hurt him in the midterms. He meant people here ten years or more without serious crimes, and said he would work with Democrats.
Miller is that policy's architect. Indiana Republican Marlin Stutzman told CNN the White House should fire people, including Miller, who he said is not liked in the Midwest.
The Dana White story is smaller, and funnier. Trump floated the U.F.C. boss as press secretary. Now he says he was only kidding. White still comes to the White House today, quote, on other matters.
In the Senate, Dave McCormick and Ron Johnson want Tuesday's Republican leadership elections delayed, until the conference has digested the midterms. No challenger to Leader Thune has been declared.

One more from that interview. Asked about U.F.O.s, Trump said he is not too much of a believer, but has talked with military pilots who say something is going on out there. Alien Joe has no comment. Alien Joe has a lot of comments.

segments.strap: JEFFRIES 'HARD YES' ON HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT; BLANCHE: DOJ 'COULD' PROBE
segments.headline: Impeachment vote looms; the attorney general's warning

graphic.title: Hegseth and the oversight fight
bullets: Jeffries: 'I'm a hard yes'; caucus meets Tuesday
Massie reintroduces eight articles, incl. War Powers
Blanche: DOJ 'could' investigate Democrats; no statute named
Alaska count frozen until Nov 18

lines.text: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said on ABC, quote, I'm a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution. He says the defense secretary should leave office. His caucus discusses it Tuesday morning.

Republican Thomas Massie says he will reintroduce his privileged resolution as early as today. It has eight articles, including a War Powers charge. Under House rules, that forces a floor vote within two legislative days. Hegseth called Massie a, quote, disgruntled, defeated congressman. CNN reports Trump defended Hegseth.
Conviction in the Senate needs two-thirds. That bar has not changed.

Meanwhile Attorney General Todd Blanche told CNN and Fox that he could investigate congressional Democrats. He named no law. Asked whether anyone goes to prison, he said it depends on what the crime is. He added, quote, I would be very worried if I was a member on that committee.
The White House posted a release calling Democratic oversight a charade. Two House Democrats have floated impeaching Blanche. Nothing has been filed or opened.

Democrats say their agenda is Medicaid cuts, the Iran war, tariffs and health care. The Guardian reports it is not Trump's impeachment. Still counting: Alaska's Senate race is frozen until November eighteenth, and the Senate stands at fifty-four to forty-four with Alaska and Mississippi open.

segments.strap: EISENKOT GETS MANDATE; TRUMP REPORTEDLY PRESSES NETANYAHU ON GAZA
segments.headline: A mandate, a clock, and a push from Washington

graphic.title: Eisenkot's 28 days
bullets: Herzog hands Eisenkot the mandate
Eisenkot: 'national emergency government'
Netanyahu warns against Arab-party partners
Axios: Trump pressed Netanyahu on Gaza plan's next phase

lines.text: Israel's president, Isaac Herzog, formally gave Gadi Eisenkot the job of forming a government. Sixty-seven lawmakers recommended Eisenkot, against forty-six for Benjamin Netanyahu. Eisenkot has twenty-eight days, with a possible fourteen more, and needs sixty-one supporters.

Herzog said the tally does not settle it, because of mutual vetoes between and within blocs. Eisenkot wants a, quote, national emergency government, with creative and unconventional steps. His party says Likud and its friends could join, but not Netanyahu.
Netanyahu posted a video warning against partners from Arab parties. Eisenkot called it hysterical. If Eisenkot fails, sixty-one lawmakers can jointly ask Herzog to name someone else.

From Washington, a claim. Axios reports that on a call after the election, Trump pressed Netanyahu to move on the next phase of the Gaza plan: Hamas disarmament and a Palestinian technocratic authority. A source called it constructive. Neither office commented. Netanyahu's public line is that Hamas is rearming.

In Gaza, heavy rain flooded the tents of about seventy thousand displaced Palestinians, aid officials say. AP reports a sandstone slab fell on tents in Deir al-Balah, killing at least four, including three children, per hospital officials.

In Amsterdam, tens of thousands marched in red against Israel's war, AP says. The organizers, Amnesty Netherlands, say more than two hundred thousand. They demand the Dutch government stop buying Israeli weapons.

segments.strap: ZAPORIZHZHIA LINE LOST, RESTORED; 600,000 DARK IN DNIPRO REGION
segments.headline: The grid is the front line, and Abu Dhabi is tomorrow

graphic.title: Power, a plant and the talks
bullets: Zaporizhzhia: IAEA counts 27th off-site power loss
Three die of carbon monoxide from a generator in a basement
France says Europe will attend Abu Dhabi talks
Hackers' Rosstat leak: unverified

lines.text: Russia's strikes on Ukraine's grid left hundreds of thousands without power. Ukrainian authorities say more than six hundred thousand customers lost electricity in five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region. Hospitals ran on generators.

At the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, the last outside power line disconnected before dawn Sunday and the plant ran on emergency diesel. The U.N. nuclear agency calls it the plant's twenty-seventh loss of outside power in the war. The line was switched back on about ten hours later, Ukraine's nuclear operator says.
In Kyiv Oblast, three people, including a child, died of carbon monoxide after a generator was run inside a basement. Emergency services say that is not a strike toll.

Rescue work in Komyshuvakha is in its seventh day. Fifty-five bodies recovered, twenty-nine identified, forty-five people still listed missing. Ukrainian officials say a Russian drone hit the site again Sunday, damaging equipment. Nobody was hurt.

Next, the talks. U.S., Russian and Ukrainian delegations meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday. France's foreign minister says Europeans will take part, and he could not yet name who will represent France. Trump told 60 Minutes Ukraine will, quote, end up with a little bit different shape. Zelensky says territorial concession is unconstitutional.

Two claims on the other side. Ukrainian monitoring channels say drones hit the Kirishi oil refinery near St. Petersburg. The governor says one hundred thirteen drones were shot down. No damage assessment exists.

And Belarusian hackers say they stole twenty-three terabytes from Russia's statistics agency, implying up to four hundred fifty thousand war-linked deaths. The agency denies a leak. A named count by Russian journalists stands near two hundred eighty-six thousand. Unverified.

A footnote: viral alerts last week warned Ukrainians and Russians of imminent chemical and nuclear attacks. They were fake messages pushed through hacked emergency apps, in a story from the first days of November. Nothing new on who did it.

segments.strap: KRAKÓW GUNMAN DIES IN HOSPITAL; TERRORISM INVESTIGATION OPEN
segments.headline: What is new in Kraków

graphic.title: After the Main Square shooting
bullets: Police: suspect died Monday morning in hospital
Prosecutors treat it as a terrorist offence
Interior minister: suspect fascinated by far-right ideologies
Two police officers who stopped him were conscious Sunday

lines.text: An update on Kraków. Polish police posted Monday morning that the perpetrator of the tragic events died that morning in the hospital. He was a twenty-four-year-old Polish man, per most reports. The Guardian says twenty-five.

Six people died in the Main Square: four women and two men, among them a British man and an Austrian woman. Three more bodies, his parents and his sister, police say, were found at the family home. More than a dozen were wounded.

Prosecutors are treating the square as a terrorist offence and say the evidence points to the same person at both places. They are preparing six murder charges, which could become nine. Those are the prosecutors' words.

The interior minister said the man was fascinated by far-right ideologies, and a ministry spokesperson says many different emblems are being analyzed. Those are officials' statements, not a court finding. The city is in mourning through Wednesday.

segments.strap: FRANCE WAGE TALKS TODAY; STORM BRUNA HITS MADEIRA; ERDOĞAN IN KARABAKH
segments.headline: Europe and the U.K.

graphic.title: Paris, Madeira, the Caucasus
bullets: Lecornu meets unions and employers on wages
Unions ask for 80 to 150 euros net; labour minister wants 1,500
Madeira: lifeguard missing; two cruise calls lost
Reuters exclusive: EU report says Russian network exploited French riots (claim)

lines.text: France. Prime Minister Lecornu receives unions and employers at his office this morning to answer on wages. The net minimum wage is one thousand four hundred seventy-eight euros. The CGT wants about ten percent. The CFDT wants one hundred euros more. The labour minister wants to cross fifteen hundred. No outcome had been reported when the capture closed.

A claim from Reuters: an exclusive says an E.U. report finds a covert Russian network exploited the recent riots in France on social media. Reuters's headline was the only version seen. No details were opened.

In Portugal, Storm Bruna hit Madeira. The regional civil protection service logged one hundred forty-five incidents in a day, including fallen trees and floods. Nine people were displaced, and a lifeguard is missing. Twenty flights were cancelled Sunday, and two cruise calls were lost.

In the Caucasus, Turkey's president, Erdoğan, visited Karabakh with Azerbaijan's Aliyev. A regional outlet says Aliyev told reporters a peace text with Armenia was initialed more than a year ago and is not yet signed. That is that outlet's report.
In Britain, King Charles led the solemn Remembrance service at the Cenotaph. And Starbucks plans to hire seventy-five hundred people in the U.K.

segments.strap: POPE: 'ECONOMY MUST SERVE PEOPLE'; PARAGUAY'S PRESIDENT HELD
segments.headline: Pope in Argentina, a president in custody, a cartel arrest

graphic.title: Buenos Aires, Asunción, Mexico
bullets: Pope: 'The economy must be at the service of people'
Judge orders Peña held pending trial; he denies wrongdoing
Mexico arrests alleged CJNG cell leader 'R2'
Rio state: 10 dead in car in lake, five children

lines.text: Pope Leo landed in Buenos Aires on Sunday and was greeted by President Milei. In his address at Palacio Libertad he said, quote, the economy must be at the service of people, and not people at the service of the economy.

The Guardian calls the speech a rebuke of Milei's austerity and reads one line as a reference to cuts. That reading is the paper's. The Vatican's own text did not name him. The pope stays through Wednesday, then goes to Peru.

In Paraguay, a judge ordered President Santiago Peña held in pretrial detention at a military barracks in Asunción, citing flight and obstruction. It follows the collapse of the bank ueno. The charges are breach of trust and administration for personal gain. Peña denies wrongdoing. His lawyer says he will plead not guilty. This is not a conviction.
The former central bank chief, Carlos Carvallo, was also ordered detained. Alliana remains sworn in as president.

In Mexico, the Navy, on intelligence from the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, arrested Rafael Alvarez, known as R2, an alleged Jalisco cartel cell leader, near Guadalajara. Twenty people were arrested in total. He is linked to at least nineteen killings, including Uruapan's mayor Carlos Manzo last year.

Separately, a kidnapped border-town mayor in Mexico was found alive after hours. And in Brazil, ten people were found dead in a car that plunged into a lake in Barra Mansa, Rio de Janeiro state. The state government says five were children. The cause is under investigation.

segments.strap: ANC WORST-EVER VOTE; EGYPT TRAIN CRASH 7 DEAD; SENEGAL BOAT 21+ DEAD
segments.headline: Africa

graphic.title: Elections and disasters
bullets: Johannesburg: DA leads, no majority
Giza: rear-end train collision; 112 hurt
Senegal pirogue sank off Lompoul
Sudan re-detains ICC fugitive Haroun (lawyers)

lines.text: South Africa's election commission declared the results of all two hundred thirteen local councils. The African National Congress is still the largest party but had its worst local result ever, at about thirty-one percent. The Democratic Alliance is at about twenty-five. Turnout was fifty-two percent.

Two government pages print slightly different party numbers, so treat those percentages as approximate. Both say one hundred twenty-seven councils are hung. In Johannesburg the D.A. leads with about thirty-five percent, but no party has a majority. No mayor or coalition has been announced. One voting district will revote, after ballots were destroyed.

In Egypt, two passenger trains collided south of Cairo in Giza. One struck the rear of a stopped train. The health ministry says seven people died and one hundred twelve were injured. A conductor is among the dead. President Sisi ordered an investigation.

Off Senegal, a migrant boat sank near Lompoul, about one hundred eighty kilometers north of Dakar. The interior ministry says twenty-one are dead, provisionally, with one survivor. Emergency services told AFP at least thirty-five. The numbers have not been reconciled.

In Sudan, the military has again detained Ahmed Haroun, a former Bashir-era official wanted by the International Criminal Court for Darfur crimes, in Kassala, per two defense lawyers. No reason was given.

segments.strap: DELHI SMOG AFTER DIWALI; CHINA FACTORY PRICES +5.7%; HASINA PASSPORT
segments.headline: Asia

graphic.title: Smog, prices and politics
bullets: Delhi: toxic smog; 'severe' forecast for coming days
China: consumer prices +0.7%; factory prices highest since 2022
Japan: Mitsui Chemicals, state bank to buy JSR for about $12 billion
Ex-PM Hasina asks for passport; says she will return in December

lines.text: New Delhi woke to toxic smog after Diwali fireworks. The city's air quality index averaged three hundred seventy-six on Sunday. Twenty of fifty-nine stations were in the severe category on Diwali night. The early warning system forecasts severe air through the coming days.

China's statistics bureau reports October consumer prices up seven-tenths of a percent from a year earlier, slower than September. Factory-gate prices rose five point seven percent, the largest jump since twenty twenty-two. The bureau also credits A.I. demand for rising electronics prices: storage devices up forty-five percent.

In Japan, Mitsui Chemicals and a state-backed development bank will buy JSR, the number two maker of chip photoresist, for about twelve billion dollars. Mitsui's shares fell about thirteen percent on the news. The Nikkei closed up two point two four percent.
In Bangladesh, ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's lawyers asked for a new passport, saying she will return in December and surrender to a court. She faces a death sentence in absentia.

In Malaysia, the attorney general admitted glaring drafting errors in the court order for Najib Razak's proposed house arrest. Implementation is suspended. And Typhoon Cempaka entered the Philippine area with winds of one hundred twenty kilometers an hour. The weather agency expects no direct effect on the country.

segments.strap: OIL SLIPS ON 'UNLIKELY'; ~79% ODDS OF DECEMBER FED HIKE; CPI TUESDAY
segments.headline: Markets and the week ahead

graphic.title: The week ahead
bullets: Dow futures +0.7% Sunday night after early dip
Taiwan's Taiex +4.9%
U.S. consumer prices (CPI) due Tuesday
Earnings: Occidental, Take-Two, Rocket Lab after the close

lines.text: Oil fell on Monday in Asia after Trump called new Iran strikes highly unlikely. Brent traded between about ninety-seven and ninety-eight dollars. Reuters notes it fell sixteen percent last week, the steepest weekly drop since the start of the pandemic.

Wall Street futures opened lower Sunday night, then reversed. The Dow was up about seven-tenths of a percent by late evening. Taiwan's market jumped nearly five percent behind TSMC. Friday's U.S. closes stand: the S&P 500 at seven thousand three hundred seventy-seven.

Markets are now pricing about a seventy-nine percent chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, per reports citing strong U.S. jobs data. That is a hike, not a cut. The next clue is consumer prices on Tuesday. Forecasters expect three-tenths of a percent for the headline number.
Bitcoin slid under seventy-five thousand dollars, down from above eighty thousand on Thursday. There is no weekend fund-flow report to explain it.
Today's earnings: before the open, Constellation Energy and KKR. After the close, Occidental, Rocket Lab, Take-Two, The Trade Desk and Plug Power.

segments.strap: PHILLY BOYCOTT OF JEWISH-OWNED RESTAURANTS; WINSTON-SALEM SHOOTING
segments.headline: Around the country

graphic.title: Around the country
bullets: Philly: 'Boycott Ride' met by about 500 supporters of the restaurants
Winston-Salem: homecoming cancelled; suspect held without bond
Newport Beach: fishermen rescue cruise-ship pianist 15 to 20 miles out
Mayor Parker: targeting Jewish businesses 'has no place'

lines.text: Philadelphia. A group called Philly Bike On Your Left held a Boycott Ride targeting six Jewish-owned restaurants near Rittenhouse Square, over what it called their support for Israel. About five hundred people turned out in support of the restaurants. One arrest was reported.

Mayor Cherelle Parker said the targeting of Jewish-owned businesses has no place in Philadelphia. The state attorney general called it discrimination. The Jewish Federation objected to the date, the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht.

In North Carolina, shots on the Winston-Salem State University campus during homecoming Saturday night. Police say a nineteen-year-old man died. A twenty-two-year-old woman was treated and released. A twenty-year-old is held without bond on a murder charge. Local outlets count more people shot in two separate incidents. Homecoming was cancelled.

And one with a good ending. Two fishermen returning from Catalina found a man treading water fifteen to twenty miles off Newport Beach. He is a pianist on a Royal Caribbean ship, and says he was in the water about nine hours. He is expected to survive. The Coast Guard is investigating how he went overboard.

segments.strap: ATMOSPHERIC RIVERS HIT PACIFIC NORTHWEST; STORM BRUNA; TYPHOON CEMPAKA
segments.headline: Weather

graphic.title: Storms on three coasts
bullets: Northwest: more atmospheric rivers late Monday into Tuesday
Southwest floods lifted Lake Powell by 20 feet
Erbil flood killed three, per the governor
Tropical Storm Pena: no land hazards

lines.text: The Pacific Northwest is in a series of atmospheric rivers. The weather service issued wind advisories for Seattle, with gusts of forty-five to fifty miles an hour in the lowlands and above ninety on mountain tops. One report counts nearly one hundred thousand Washington customers without power over the weekend.

A second storm is coming. A high wind watch is posted for the coast, with the next system arriving late Monday into Tuesday. The weather service does not expect river flooding. Fox Weather says minor flooding is possible as soils saturate.
In the Southwest, AP says late-October and early-November floods raised Lake Powell by twenty feet and sent rare inflows to drought-drained reservoirs. Hundreds of people were told to evacuate.

Elsewhere: Tropical Storm Pena in the Pacific has forty-five mile an hour winds and threatens no land. Typhoon Cempaka is passing the Philippines without a wind signal. Delhi's air and Madeira's storm are in the other segments.

segments.strap: ALCARAZ WINS PARIS; NORRIS WINS BRAZIL GP; UNITED 4-4 VILLA
segments.headline: Sports roundup

graphic.title: Sunday's results
bullets: Georgia back to No. 1 in AP Top 25
Larson wins third NASCAR Cup title
Lakers 121, Pistons 116 without Dončić
Bills at Vikings tonight, 8:15 ET

lines.text: Tennis. Carlos Alcaraz beat Ben Shelton seven-six, seven-five in under two hours to win the Paris Masters. It is his ninth Masters title. At the WTA Finals, Coco Gauff beat Jessica Pegula in three sets.

Formula One. Lando Norris won a wet São Paulo Grand Prix. Max Verstappen started at the back and finished second. Mercedes clinched the constructors' title. In NASCAR, Ryan Blaney won the Homestead finale, and Kyle Larson clinched a third Cup championship after an early engine failure for rival Chase Briscoe.

The N.F.L., Week nine. The Bengals beat the Falcons thirty-four to seventeen in Madrid. Cowboys twenty-seven, Colts twenty-three. Chiefs thirty-five, Jets twelve. Forty-Niners thirty-eight, Raiders seventeen. Texans forty-four, Chargers twenty-two. Sunday night, the Bears beat the Buccaneers twenty-seven to twenty-four on a game-ending field goal.
Tonight, the Bills visit the Vikings at eight-fifteen Eastern. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring, and Carson Wentz is expected to start. The trade deadline is Tuesday at four.
College football. Georgia is number one again in the A.P. poll after beating Ole Miss forty-two to seven. Utah is second and Notre Dame third. Miami, after its first loss, is fifth.

Basketball and soccer. The Lakers beat the Pistons one twenty-one to one sixteen without Luka Dončić, who sat with back tightness. Austin Reaves scored forty-three. In England, Manchester United and Aston Villa drew four-four, and United stays in the relegation zone. Liverpool won three-one at Crystal Palace.

lines.text: The U.N. climate summit, COP31, opened in Antalya, Turkey. It runs through November twentieth, with leaders speaking on the eleventh and twelfth. Opening day produced no agreement.
At the box office, Godzilla Minus Zero opened to thirty-one point six million dollars in North America, a record for a foreign-language film there, per AP's studio estimates.

Billionaire Leon Black sued Representative Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on House Oversight, for defamation over televised remarks tying Black to Epstein. Black says he cut ties in twenty eighteen. Garcia's office had not responded. Elvis Presley's and Eminem's rights holders sued the A.I. music generator Suno over alleged music cloning.
NASA opened applications for its next astronaut class, with a focus on living and working on the Moon. A launch from Vandenberg, USSF six twenty-seven, is set for tonight on a Falcon Nine.

Health. The C.D.C. counts five thousand one hundred eighty-two U.S. measles cases as of November fifth. On Ebola, a tracker citing Congo's institute reports about ten thousand nine hundred confirmed cases. Those figures differ from W.H.O.'s, which uses a different cutoff.

Press reports say Apple is working to make Siri more agentic. A finance column says Anthropic's stock listing is racing for a debut before Thanksgiving. Nothing from the company itself. Treat that as talk. And the Elvis-and-Eminem lawsuit is a good reminder that Alien Joe cannot be cloned. Believe me, they tried.
